reason: Candidate C1 is the strongest hypothesis because it directly addresses the specific problem of room-temperature brittleness in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) by proposing a concrete, physically consistent mechanism: Stepwise Controllable Coherent Nanoprecipitation (SCCP). It explicitly details the intervention (two-stage heat treatment), the structural mediator (5-20 nm coherent precipitates), and the mechanism (dislocation transmission vs. Orowan looping) which is specific to the system described. Crucially, it provides quantified predictions (YS > 1.0 GPa, ductility > 10%) and a decisive falsification experiment that isolates the variable of 'coherency' by comparing the proposed route against a standard aging route designed to produce incoherent precipitates.
